t: Linker - Signature build-tool concept
title: Linker - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Combines compiled object files and libraries into a program.
description:
The Signature Linker exists to combines compiled object files and libraries into a program. It is one of the fundamental capabilities in the AI build-tool catalog: the set of tools, engines and disciplines an AI needs to design, engineer, generate, test and deliver things on demand. Where public tools each solve a slice of the problem, the Signature line defines the whole capability as a coherent framework with contracts between its parts.

Consider what happens without a disciplined Linker. Linker work degrades into folklore - tricks that work on one machine, steps remembered differently by every practitioner, failures nobody can reproduce. The Signature framework answers with determinism: declared inputs, explicit transformations, verified outputs, and an audit trail that explains every result. The pillars below are the machinery that makes that promise concrete.

This is a Signature-concept database: the framework it describes is the Signature line's own design, labeled as such throughout. The techniques and standards records cite real public knowledge; the pillars and drills are the Signature system's original construction. All of it ships with runnable demos, because in the Signature line a tool proves itself by running.

t: Signature Kernel - Linker framework pillar
title: Signature Kernel - Linker framework pillar
definition: The Kernel component of the Signature Linker framework, owning kernel. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Linker framework, the Kernel owns the framework's kernel responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Kernel's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Kernel from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Combines compiled object files and libraries into a program.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Programming languages and runtimes build needs Linker, so the framework invokes the Kernel on the the framework's kernel responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Linker. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Evaluator - Linker framework pillar
title: Signature Evaluator - Linker framework pillar
definition: The Evaluator component of the Signature Linker framework, owning evaluator. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Linker framework decomposes the capability (Combines compiled object files and libraries into a program.) into seven pillars, and the Evaluator is the one that owns the framework's evaluator responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Linker result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Evaluator's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Evaluator's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Linker. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Collector - Linker framework pillar
title: Signature Collector - Linker framework pillar
definition: The Collector component of the Signature Linker framework, owning collector. Signature concept.
description:
The Collector is a load-bearing component of the Signature Linker framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's collector responsibilities belongs to the Collector, and the Collector answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Collector can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Collector works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Linker charter (combines compiled object files and libraries into a program.). The Collector reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small languages job that needs Linker. The Collector takes the request's collector responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Collector's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.
